item.text: Two detection cases need attention: `cache.memory.enabled` is checked by value, so an explicit `false` is missed; `cache.memory.expiration` can appear set through the alias or default path. The UI fixture already includes `enabled: false`, which gives a concrete case for the missing warning. I’m running the existing config tests with network access disabled, then I’ll record the diagnosis.

item.text:
The fault is in [config.go](/app/internal/config/config.go:38): `Load` returns `*Config`, and `prepare` writes warnings into `Config.Warnings` after defaults begin. The requested `Result{Config, Warnings}` needs warning collection from keys explicitly present in the file before defaults are applied.

Likely change points are [cache.go](/app/internal/config/cache.go:52), where a value check misses an explicit `cache.memory.enabled: false` and `IsSet` can include defaulted values; [database.go](/app/internal/config/database.go:59), which also uses `IsSet`; and [ui.go](/app/internal/config/ui.go:10), which has no deprecation check. The production caller in [main.go](/app/cmd/flipt/main.go:162) must read the result and log its warnings. Existing [tests](/app/internal/config/config_test.go:224) assert warnings inside `Config` and will need to distinguish file keys from environment values.

One scope uncertainty remains: [http.go](/app/internal/cmd/http.go:111) still uses `UI.Enabled` to gate UI routes, while the stated requirements explicitly call for a deprecation warning, not a runtime change. The existing config tests pass on the unmodified checkout. I recorded the diagnosis in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`; the developer’s fault-localization scope prohibited editing project source or tests, so the requested fix is not implemented.
